title: Rapid stabilization sprint play notes
content:
Purpose: quick reference notes and decisions from the 2024-11-01 -> 2024-11-12 rapid stabilization sprint. This is a working doc (not final) capturing triage outcomes, owner skips, mitigation scripts, and short-term playbook changes to reduce mean time to recovery for mid-release regressions.

Context summary:
- Release: r2024.11.0 deployed 2024-10-29 to staging and 2024-10-31 to canary region eu-west1. Several regressions surfaced during canary traffic between 11:00–15:00 UTC on 2024-10-31 (latency tail spikes, redis connection churn under load, two model-variant fallbacks misrouted).
- Business impact: degraded latency for low-traffic premium customers (~3 customers flagged), potential SLA risk if not contained; no data leakage or model integrity issues observed.
- Sprint goal (this doc): contain regressions, validate roll-forward candidate, rebuild canary gating checks, and author 2 tactical runbooks for next incidents.

Meeting notes (standup cadence daily 09:30 PT):
- 2024-11-01: triage and owner assignments. Miguel (infra) to isolate redis churn, Avery (serving-runtime) to reproduce kv cache misroute, Samir (release) to freeze change queue, Priya to lead customer comms draft.
- 2024-11-03: infra found an interaction between connection pooling and soft-reconnect backoff when burst > 600 rps; mitigation applied: reduce max connection attempts and enable jittered backoff (hotpatch). Observed 40% reduction in reconnects in lab.
- 2024-11-05: serving-runtime discovered failure mode when KV cache prefetcher raced with model swap; introduced an instrumentation flag to force sequential prefetch in canary for next 48h.
- 2024-11-08: canary restart window — monitored 12 hours, no recurrence on eu-west1 with smaller batch sizes. Identified one config drift on trial clusters: batching.max_tokens = 4096 vs expected 2048.
- 2024-11-11: decision to roll-forward r2024.11.1 with two immediate safeguards: connection backoff tweak and prefetch sequential flag. Rollout window: 2024-11-13 02:00–06:00 UTC with canary gating and automated rollback on 3s client P50 increase or 25% increase in reconnect rate.

Actions and owners (short):
- Miguel O.: ship infra hotpatch (connection backoff + jitter) — ACTION: infra/hotpatch-20241101 — due 2024-11-12 — status: done in canary, pending prod rollout.
- Avery C.: merge serving-runtime instrumentation + prefetch flag (PR #789) — ACTION: infra#789 — due 2024-11-12 — status: merged to canary branch.
- Samir P.: update deployment gates and alert thresholds in rollout pipeline (add reconnect-rate metric to gate) — ACTION: pipeline/GATE-14 — due 2024-11-12 — status: in progress.
- Priya N.: draft customer comms and operational note for CS — ACTION: cs/notice-20241101 — due 2024-11-13 — status: draft 0.6.
- Elena K.: runbook authoring — rapid-rollback checklist + post-incident eval template — ACTION: runbook/RR-quick — due 2024-11-15 — status: in_review.

Playbook changes proposed (short-term, tactical):
1) Canary gating additions:
   - Add reconnect-rate (redis reconnects per minute) as a hard gate. Threshold = baseline * 3 for first 30m, reduce to baseline * 1.5 after 2h.
   - Add P50/P95 client-observed latency delta over baseline as a gate: immediate rollback if P50 > +3s or P95 > +7s sustained for 10m.
2) Rapid isolation heuristic:
   - If reconnect-rate spike observed, immediately disable autoscaling for affected pools (prevents noisy neighbors) and limit new allocations.
   - If KV cache misroute suspected, toggle prefetch sequential flag and restart one replica at a time with 2m spacing.
3) Hotfix packaging: single-file manifest including: infra-hotpatch.sh, serving-runtime-flag.json, manifest-checksum.txt. This reduces partial deploy drift.

Longer-term decisions (discussion notes):
- Need a small dedicated test harness that can emulate churny connections to redis and simulate redis-miss cascades (owner: infra research).
- Consider adding an explicit canary traffic shape that stresses caching and connection churn once per release cycle.
- Explore intent to formalize a "rollback safety net" service that can intercept outbound model-routing decisions and force vendor-compatibility fallback without full service restart. (Design spike: Q1 2025)

Unresolved questions / open risks:
- How many customers should we proactively notify for a transient canary-only regression? (CS asks: top 5 vs all affected premium?)
- Can we measure reconnect-rate accurately at the proxy layer vs application client? Gap: we currently sample reconnects in app logs; need a proxy-level metric.
- Are there any downstream scheduled data pipeline jobs that assume consistent batching.max_tokens? (prod jobs might fail silently)

Quick diagnostics snippets (copyable):
- Count redis reconnects in logs (last 1h): grep -c "redis.*reconnect" /var/log/serving/*.log || use splunk query: index=prod component=serving "redis reconnect" | stats count by host
- Enable sequential prefetch flag (canary only): curl -X POST $CANARY_CONFIG_URL -d '{"kv_prefetch_sequential":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Rollback heuristic (manual): trigger rollback job: ./deploy/rollback.sh --to-tag r2024.10.9 --force-checks

After-action notes (so far):
- The jittered backoff change had immediate effect in canary. Should reduce incident rate for similar bursts. Need to confirm across regions.
- Prefetch flag removes race but has a small perf cost (~3% tokens/sec). Tradeoff accepted for safety until we root-cause the prefetch scheduling race.

Lessons learned / notes to file for retrospective:
- Small config drifts (batching.max_tokens) are low-noise but high-impact when combined with adaptive batching heuristics. Need an automated config-drift scanner that checks critical runtime config across clusters pre-rollout.
- Instrumentation gaps: reconnect-rate should be first-order metric for any infra that talks to stateful stores.
- Deploy complexity: bundling small cross-repo fixes into a single manifest reduces partial deploys.

Appendix: short timeline (compact)
- 2024-10-31 11:00 UTC — first latency spike in eu-west1 canary; CS ticket opened by customer A.
- 2024-11-01 — triage; owners assigned.
- 2024-11-03 — infra hotpatch to jittered backoff applied to canary.
- 2024-11-05 — serving-runtime prefetch instrumentation candidate built.
- 2024-11-08 — canary observation window (12h).
- 2024-11-11 — roll-forward decision for r2024.11.1 in planned window 2024-11-13.

Notes to self / scratch (don't delete):
- Check with SRE on alert noise if we add reconnect gate; need escalation path without paging when transient.
- Follow up: schedule a 45m deep-dive with infra + serving runtime to map lifecycle of KV prefetch (owner: Avery).

End of working notes. Will update after rollout and final post-incidence review.
